probe: cutlery arm-assignment A/B, unattended cron tick 2026-09-09T17:00Z
row_under_test: req_demo_video (DRAFT) -- its blocker is task_success 0/20, and envs/task.py scores task_success as all(sg.values()), so spoon_placed=0 caps it by itself
question: evidence/grasp_feasibility.json measured the SCRIPTED arm-to-cutlery pairing as the worse of the two available assignments on BOTH items. Does swapping it place the cutlery?

the_prediction_being_tested.basis: evidence/grasp_feasibility.json cross_summary -- median lowest height above the grasp site at which the solved pose is collision-free; larger means the arm must stop further away
the_prediction_being_tested.reading: the swap improves the predicted clearance on both items, 18->8 and 40->30, and CUTLERY_DESCEND_Z is 0.003 so every descent is commanded well inside its own collision
the_prediction_being_tested.geometry: the spoon sits at y=0.128 and the fork at y=0.178, so the spoon is the item nearer the drawer FRONT rail, and drawer_front is what blocks it. The two objects are otherwise byte-identical in the scene -- same handle box (0.006 0.038 0.0025), same head, same mass, same friction.

method: Two arms, same 20 seeds, same scorer, same policy, privileged scene, --no-render, paired per seed. envs/task.py and the randomizer untouched. The knob is envs/controller.py CUTLERY_ARM_SWAP.

A_shipped.per_subgoal_note: every sub-goal is listed explicitly, including the zeros. The counter that produced these tallies only TRUE outcomes, so a sub-goal that never fires would otherwise be absent from the record and read as 'not measured' rather than as the zero it is -- and spoon_placed, the headline of this file, is exactly such a key.

knob_default_is_inert.how: With the knob unset the 20-seed run reproduces 32/100 and the per-seed column [3,2,3,1,1,1,1,2,2,2,1,2,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,2] EXACTLY -- the same column evidence/cutlery_direct_place_ab.json pinned for its own A_shipped arm on a different tick. A 2-seed run before the 20-seed one gave 3 and 2 from the same column.
knob_default_is_inert.why_it_matters: the edit substitutes variables for the arm-name literals on the shipped path; if that path had drifted, both columns would be measuring a different robot

scorer_untouched.how: envs/task.py has no edit this tick

the_swap_actually_took_effect.how: drawer_open, plate_placed and mug_placed all move discordant seeds between the arms (1, 5 and 2 respectively), so arm B is demonstrably a different rollout and not a no-op that would trivially reproduce A

what_it_shows: The swap does not place the spoon. spoon_placed 0/20 -> 0/20 with ZERO discordant seeds -- not one seed of twenty changed on the target sub-goal.
It is worse on the aggregate: 32/100 -> 30/100, better on 2 seeds and worse on 3.

Predicted grasp-pose clearance does not drive cutlery placement. The swap improved the predicted clearance on both items and moved neither: fork_placed 3 -> 3 (2 gained, 2 lost) and spoon_placed 0 -> 0.
The losses land on sub-goals the swap was not aimed at -- drawer_open and plate_placed -- which is the crossing-arm cost the direct-place probe also paid.
what_it_does_NOT_show: It does not show the shipped pairing is optimal. It shows the ALTERNATIVE is not better, on this scorer at n=20; the aggregate sign test is p=1.0 (2 better, 3 worse, 15 tied), which is not a difference in either direction.
It does not refute evidence/grasp_feasibility.json, whose numbers are plan-only and were reproduced, not re-measured here. What it refutes is the inference FROM them to placement.
It says nothing about task_success, which is 0/20 in both arms.
adoption: NOT ADOPTED. CUTLERY_ARM_SWAP ships at '0' and the emitted moves at that default are the shipped ones. No published number changes, so nothing downstream needs reconciling.
what_this_closes: The arm assignment is now the THIRD independent intervention to leave spoon_placed exactly invariant with zero discordant seeds, after the hand-off (evidence/cutlery_direct_place_ab.json) and the spoon's position (evidence/spoon_depth.json). That convergence is what motivated evidence/spoon_hold.json, which measured the assumption all three share.
next_step: See evidence/spoon_hold.json. It falsifies the premise this file inherited -- that the spoon is never in anybody's jaws -- and splits spoon_placed=0 into two separate failures with different fixes.
